nonop.text: ◦ Noninterest expense decreased 1%, driven by the impact of efficiency initiatives, including an 8% reduction in headcount, lower severance expense, and lower lease expense, partially offset by higher revenue-related compensation expense reflecting improved performance and an increase in technology and equipment expense. Third quarter 2025 included $296 million of severance expense

net sales.heading: ◦ Revenue increased 5%
net sales.text:
▪ Consumer, Small and Business Banking was up 7% driven by higher deposit balances, wider deposit spreads, as well as higher deposit-related fees, investment advisory fees, and debit card fees on higher volume

▪ Credit Card was up 3% reflecting higher net interest income on higher loan balances and higher card fees

▪ Home Lending was down 15% due to lower mortgage servicing income and lower net interest income on lower loan balances

▪ Auto was up 33% due to higher loan balances and wider loan spreads

◦ Noninterest expense decreased 3% driven by lower operating costs and operating losses, as well as the impact of efficiency initiatives, partially offset by higher revenue-related compensation expense and higher occupancy expense

Commercial Banking provides financial solutions to private, family owned and certain public companies. Products and services include banking and credit products across multiple industry sectors and municipalities, secured lending and lease products, and treasury management.

intro.text: Wells Fargo & Company (NYSE: WFC) is a leading financial services company that has approximately $2.3 trillion in assets. We provide a diversified set of banking, investment and mortgage products and services, as well as consumer and commercial finance, through our four reportable operating segments: Consumer Banking and Lending, Commercial Banking, Corporate and Investment Banking, and Wealth & Investment Management. Wells Fargo ranked No. 38 on Fortune’s 2026 rankings of America’s largest corporations.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
